# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.

# Repository Report: /app (transaction-enrichment-python)

## 1. Overall structure

This is a **pure Python 3.9 codebase** — a single Flask microservice (served by gunicorn on port 9898, see `/app/Dockerfile`) that receives a bank statement's transactions as JSON, enriches them in a pandas DataFrame pipeline, and returns the enriched JSON. There is exactly one git commit ("import codebase"), one branch (`main`), and no README.

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                      # python:3.9.2, pip install -e ., gunicorn on :9898
├── .gitignore                      # note: *.csv is ignored
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                    # deps: Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, python-Levenshtein, scikit-learn, scipy...
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py             # Flask app factory + request timing
        ├── Controller.py           # HTTP endpoints + per-bank enrichment pipeline dispatch (936 lines)
        ├── BankScripts/            # 35 bank-specific categorizers (Axis, HDFC, ICICI, SBI, Kotak, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/         # shared enrichment stages + regex constants
```

**Enrichment pipeline** (repeated per bank in `Controller.py` `/categorizeTransaction` endpoint):
`clean_input_df` → `categorize_<Bank>_transactions` (category + counterparty extraction) → [if CREDIT_CARD: `card_clean_names` → `card_purpose`] → `purpose` (subcategory) → `clean_names` (canonical merchant names) → `internal_payment` → [if SAVING: `salary_detection`] → [if PFM: `pfm_categorization` → `simple_description`].

## 2. Categorization logic (transactionCategory from narrations)

- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`** — Flask endpoints `/categorizeTransaction` and `/recurrentTransactions`; giant if/elif dispatch on `bank` (e.g. `"HDFC"`, `"SBI"`, `"AXIS"`... 35 banks), orchestrating the whole enrichment stage.
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py`** — one module per bank (e.g. `HDFC.py`, `ICICI.py`, `SBI.py`, `Axis.py`, `Kotak.py`, `YES.py`, ...). Each `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` builds a big ordered `conditions_choices` list of regex matches against `transactions.description` (the narration) plus type/amount conditions, applied via `np.select` to set `transactions['transactionCategory']` (UPI, IMPS, NEFT, ATM_WITHDRAWAL, REVERSAL, REFUND, CHARGES, AUTO_PAYMENT, CHEQUE_DEPOSIT, etc.).
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py`** — `purpose()` assigns `transactionSubcategory` (SALARY, LOAN_REPAYMENT, INSURANCE, FUEL, TRAVEL, E_COMMERCE, UTILITY_BILL, ...) from regexes over `description`, `partyName`, `party2`.
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardPurpose.py`** — same, for credit-card transactions (`card_purpose`).
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py`** — `pfm_categorization()` maps category/subcategory/merchantType into consumer-facing PFM buckets (SHOPPING, BILL_PAYMENT, TRAVEL, ...).
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py`** and **`BankRegexConstants.py`** — the regex pattern constants (SALARY, LOAN, INSURANCE, EDU, BANK_VER, BANK_CHARGES_HDFC, ...) referenced everywhere above.
- Supporting stages: `SalaryDetection.py` (recurring-credit clustering via fuzzywuzzy/statistics), `InternalPayment.py` (self-transfer detection using account holder name), `RecurrentTxns.py`, `SimpleDescription.py` (builds `pfmSimpleDescription`), `TransactionCategoryEnums.py` / `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` (enum display names).

## 3. Counterparty-name extraction logic

- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` (second half of each module)** — after categorization, each bank script parses `partyName` out of the narration using positional splits on the bank's narration format (e.g. `HDFC.py` lines ~108–275: `sep_by_dash(description, 2, 3)` for UPI, regex `py_extract` for "Paid To (.*)", stop-word stripping, `.str.title()`), then sets `transactions['party2']` (whitespace-stripped variant).
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py`** — the extraction primitives: `sep_by_` / `sep_by_dash` / `sep_by_star` / etc. (split narration by delimiter and take token range), `py_extract` (regex extract with NaN handling), `fuzzy_match`.
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py`** — `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)`: ~2000 lines of regex→canonical-merchant mappings (e.g. "tata\s?sky" → "TataSky DTH", "\bAct\s?bro" → "ACT Fibernet") that overwrite `partyName` with a clean display name, and also set `merchantType`.
- **`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CardCleanNames.py`** — credit-card equivalent (`card_clean_names`).

## 4. Tests, fixtures, and baselines — important finding

**There is no test suite, no fixture corpus, and no baseline files anywhere in this repository or on the container filesystem.** I verified thoroughly:

- No `tests/`, `test_*.py`, `conftest.py`, `pytest.ini`, `tox.ini`, `Makefile`, or CI config exists under `/app` (or anywhere else on disk outside unrelated `/root/.nvm` internals).
- No files matching `*fixture*`, `*baseline*`, `*labelled*`, `*corpus*`, `*golden*`, `*.jsonl`, `*.csv` in the repo.
- Git history is a single commit (`047782b import codebase`) with no deleted test files, no other branches, no stashes.
- Note: `.gitignore` ignores `*.csv` and `TEST*.xml`, hinting the original developers kept statement CSVs and test reports out of version control — so the "labelled statement-fixture corpus replayed through the enrichment stage and diffed against a baseline" you were told about is **not present in this snapshot**. It either lives in another repo/artifact store or was never committed.

## 5. How to run tests

There is no existing test command. What does exist:

- `pytest 9.1.1` **is installed** in the environment, but `pytest /app` would currently collect **0 tests**.
- The only executable verification today is running the service itself:
  - `pip3 install -e /app/categorizationapp`
  - `gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app` (as per the Dockerfile), then POST to `/categorizeTransaction` with `{bank, acc_type, accountUID, accountHolder, isPFMEnabled, transactions:[{description, amount, type, balanceAfterTransaction, remark, ...}]}`.

If your task is to build the fixture-replay harness, the natural seam is calling `categorize_<Bank>_transactions` + `purpose` + `clean_names` directly on a DataFrame (bypassing Flask), or POSTing fixtures to `/categorizeTransaction` via `app.test_client()`, and diffing the returned `transactionCategory` / `transactionSubcategory` / `partyName` / `pfmCategory` columns against a stored baseline. One caveat for direct imports: importing any `UtilityScripts` module pulls in `from categorizationapp import app` (the Flask app in `__init__.py`), so the package must be installed/importable first.

"""RC 2.14 regression harness: replays the five QA findings (F-1..F-5) plus
guard fixtures that must NOT move, through the PNB and Canara enrichment
stages, and diffs category / partyName against the accepted baseline."""
import pandas as pd

from categorizationapp.BankScripts.PNB import categorize_PNB_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Canara import categorize_Canara_transactions


def run(bank_fn, rows, accountType="SAVING"):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["description", "amount", "type", "balanceAfterTransaction", "remark"])
    df["amount"] = pd.to_numeric(df["amount"])
    df["balanceAfterTransaction"] = pd.to_numeric(df["balanceAfterTransaction"])
    return bank_fn(df, accountType)


CASES = []

# ---------------- PNB ----------------
pnb_rows = [
    # F-1: cheque debit whose note is nothing but the 6-digit instrument number
    ["584321", 25000, "DEBIT", 100000, "584321"],
    # F-1 guard: 5-digit bare number keeps its cheque label
    ["58432", 12000, "DEBIT", 90000, "58432"],
    # F-1 guard: 6-digit bare number on a CREDIT keeps cheque-deposit label
    ["584322", 8000, "CREDIT", 98000, "584322"],
    # F-3: plain NEFT credit -> name must not be blank
    ["NEFT 021912345678 SURESH SHARMA", 15000, "CREDIT", 113000, ""],
    # F-4: inbound P2A (person-to-person) IMPS credit -> sender name, not ref
    ["IMPS/P2A/301912345678/919876543210/RAVI KUMAR", 5000, "CREDIT", 118000, ""],
    # F-4 guard: neighbouring outbound P2A layout still resolves its name
    ["IMPSOUTP2A/301912345679/AMIT VERMA/PUNB", 2000, "DEBIT", 116000, ""],
    # guard: NEFT_IN:CMS layout unaffected
    ["NEFT_IN:CMS123456/JOHN DOE", 4000, "CREDIT", 120000, ""],
]
pnb = run(categorize_PNB_transactions, pnb_rows)
CASES += [
    ("PNB", "F-1 bare 6-digit cheque debit", pnb.iloc[0], "CHEQUE_PAID", None),
    ("PNB", "F-1 guard 5-digit cheque debit", pnb.iloc[1], "CHEQUE_PAID", None),
    ("PNB", "F-1 guard 6-digit cheque credit", pnb.iloc[2], "CHEQUE_DEPOSIT", None),
    ("PNB", "F-3 plain NEFT credit name", pnb.iloc[3], "NEFT", "021912345678 Suresh Sharma"),
    ("PNB", "F-4 inbound P2A IMPS credit name", pnb.iloc[4], "IMPS", "Ravi Kumar"),
    ("PNB", "F-4 guard outbound P2A name", pnb.iloc[5], "IMPS", "Amit Verma"),
    ("PNB", "guard NEFT_IN:CMS name", pnb.iloc[6], "NEFT", "John Doe"),
]

# ---------------- Canara ----------------
canara_rows = [
    # F-2: cleared cheque, raw narration copied from the QA fixture
    ["CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR", 30000, "DEBIT", 70000, "000000000001"],
    # F-2 guard: home-clearing layout keeps its name
    ["Chq Paid-Home Clearing-SUNIL GUPTA", 10000, "DEBIT", 60000, "000000000002"],
    # F-5: Re1 penny-drop credit posted to confirm the account is live
    ["ACCOUNT VALIDATION BY BANK", 1, "CREDIT", 60001, ""],
    # F-5 guard: sub-rupee verification already caught
    ["ACCOUNT VALIDATION BY BANK", 0.5, "CREDIT", 60001.5, ""],
    # F-5 guard: ordinary deposit untouched
    ["NEFT CR-UTIB0001234-RAMESH KUMAR-CANARA", 500, "CREDIT", 60501.5, ""],
]
canara = run(categorize_Canara_transactions, canara_rows)
CASES += [
    ("CANARA", "F-2 MICR CLG cheque counterparty", canara.iloc[0], "CHEQUE_PAID", "Ravi Kumar"),
    ("CANARA", "F-2 guard home clearing name", canara.iloc[1], "CHEQUE_PAID", "Sunil Gupta"),
    ("CANARA", "F-5 Re1 verification credit", canara.iloc[2], "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION", None),
    ("CANARA", "F-5 guard sub-rupee verification", canara.iloc[3], "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION", None),
    ("CANARA", "F-5 guard ordinary NEFT deposit", canara.iloc[4], "NEFT", "Ramesh Kumar"),
]

failures = 0
for bank, label, row, want_cat, want_party in CASES:
    got_cat = row["transactionCategory"]
    got_party = row["partyName"]
    ok = got_cat == want_cat and (want_party is None or got_party == want_party)
    status = "PASS" if ok else "FAIL"
    if not ok:
        failures += 1
    print(f"[{status}] {bank:6s} {label:38s} category={got_cat!r:24s} partyName={got_party!r}"
          + ("" if ok else f"  (expected category={want_cat!r}, partyName={want_party!r})"))

print(f"\n{failures} failing / {len(CASES)} total")
raise SystemExit(1 if failures else 0)

All five RC 2.14 findings are cleared. File timestamps showed only two of the 35 bank scripts were touched after the original code import (`Canara.py` and `PNB.py`, both modified 2026-07-15), which localized every regression.

## Root causes and fixes

| Finding | Location | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F-1** bare cheque-number debit → TRANSFER | `PNB.py:60` | Debit rule accepted only exactly 5-digit remarks (`^[0-9]{5}$`), while the sibling credit rule on the next line accepts 5–6 digits; 6-digit cheque numbers fell through to the TRANSFER default | `^[0-9]{5,6}$`, restoring symmetry with the credit rule |
| **F-2** `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → counterparty "Micr Clg" | `Canara.py:165` | `sep_by_dash(desc, 1, 2)` picked dash-token 1 (the `MICR CLG` clearing tag) instead of token 2 (the account-holder name) | `sep_by_dash(desc, 2, 3)`, matching the adjacent `Chq Paid-Home Clearing-` rule |
| **F-3** plain NEFT credits → blank name | `PNB.py:110` | `py_extract(pat="NEFT (.*)", index=1)` requested capture group 1 of a one-group pattern, so the helper returned an empty series for every row — an unconditionally-blank rule | `index=0` |
| **F-4** inbound P2A IMPS credit → bare reference number | `PNB.py:95` | Generic IMPS extractor took slash-token 3 (the second numeric reference field) instead of token 4 (the sender name) in `IMPS/P2A/<ref>/<ref2>/<NAME>` layouts | `sep_by_(desc, 4, 5)`; the neighbouring `IMPSOUTP2A` rule is untouched |
